cutoff_window.qualification_rule: Only public sources with direct visible publication or update dates inside the strict two-day window were included. Missing, ambiguous, future-dated, older, lower-bound-only, or snippet-only dates were excluded.

federation_boundary.local_owner_scope: AI-assisted development practice: context architecture, source workflows, instructions, agent workflows, coding practices, retrieval and tools, verification/evals, application patterns, governance/risk, and adoption/operating model.
federation_boundary.collector_action: Recorded practice implications and routing notes only; did not update docs/wiki or raw/processed.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenAI shares internal coding-agent adoption and measurement snapshot
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI reported that its researchers are using coding agents throughout the day, often in concurrent sessions. The post describes increased delegation across research phases, higher technical-help and monitoring use, and continued human steering needs on longer-horizon work.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice signal is to measure agent adoption by workflow taxonomy, task horizon, intervention rates, and accepted outcomes rather than raw generated-code or token volume alone.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for concurrent agent sessions, agent-work classification, and human-steering thresholds in high-complexity coding-agent workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route company and product facts upstream; keep only measurement and operating-model lessons locally.

qualifying_updates.title: Unblocked separates agent skills, rules files, and retrieved context
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Unblocked framed skills, rules files, and retrieval as separate mechanisms for shaping agent behavior, with different responsibilities for reusable procedures, durable constraints, and just-in-time repository context.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The article maps directly to local guidance on where teams should place standing instructions, task-specific procedures, and retrieved evidence so coding agents do not overload one context layer.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for instruction placement rules, context budgets, and durable skills versus retrieved repository evidence.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Avoid a local product leaf; ingest only the placement taxonomy if useful.

qualifying_updates.title: Bruin argues MCP data agents need lineage and metric definitions
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Bruin listed data-stack MCP servers and emphasized that warehouse access is not enough: agents also need lineage, column descriptions, project definitions, and authoritative metric definitions to produce reliable answers.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice update reinforces that governed MCP access must include provenance and semantic context, not just tool connectivity.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for MCP tool qualification, retrieval provenance, lineage-aware data agents, and metric-definition checks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Broad data-tool catalog details belong upstream; local wiki should keep the governance and context-contract lesson.

qualifying_updates.title: Beam distinguishes coding-agent work from unattended enterprise operations
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Beam compared developer-facing coding agents with enterprise agents by user, unit of work, runtime surface, loop shape, built-in knowledge, and governance model. It positions coding-agent output as code or pull requests that humans review and merge.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice implication is a clearer operating boundary: coding agents automate engineering sessions, while business-process agents require durable process ownership and audit controls.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for agent role boundaries, handoff expectations, and audit responsibilities across engineering and business operations.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route product comparisons upstream; local ingest can cite the operating-model distinction.

qualifying_updates.title: InfoWorld describes AI-first development as an SDLC operating model
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: InfoWorld described AI-first development as applying AI across the software development life cycle, with developers acting as architects who oversee agentic workflows. The article also highlights earlier defect surfacing, code review economics, and modernization work that clears more quickly.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice signal is that team adoption should be framed as an operating-model change with design-time quality gates, not as a selective productivity add-on.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for AI-first SDLC adoption, design-time defect gates, and developer-as-architect responsibilities.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as adoption and quality-gate evidence; avoid broad vendor background.

qualifying_updates.title: ETCIO reports build-versus-buy pressure from coding-agent adoption
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: ETCIO reported, citing McKinsey research, that AI coding agents are changing corporate technology spending by making internal software builds more attractive for some organizations, especially in technology and healthcare.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice angle is the need for explicit build-versus-buy gates that account for agent-enabled delivery speed, ownership cost, review capacity, and governance.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for agent-era build-versus-buy decision criteria and adoption economics.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Preserve the economic decision lens; do not duplicate broad McKinsey or company coverage locally.

qualifying_updates.title: Developers Digest highlights human-loop gaps in coding-agent benchmarks
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Developers Digest summarized a position paper arguing that coding-agent research over-optimizes for solo autonomy while real developer work depends on steering, verification, and adaptation inside live workflows.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice update supports evaluation designs that measure human-agent loop quality rather than only benchmark autonomy or issue-resolution rate.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for human-loop evaluation criteria, steering protocols, and workflow-representative coding-agent benchmarks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: The tag page points to the article; ingest should re-check the final article URL before moving this raw source to processed.

qualifying_updates.title: Verdent guide frames prototype validation as evidence before agent-built product expansion
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Verdent described using agents to break product goals into tasks and return outputs for review while warning that prototype task completion is not the same as validated demand or willingness to pay.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice implication is to pair agent-generated prototypes with explicit validation questions and human interpretation of evidence.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for prototype validation loops, evidence reviews, and product-decision boundaries around agent-built prototypes.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep the product-validation workflow; route Verdent product background upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: Verdent guide treats software delivery agents as dependency, blocker, and review coordinators
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Verdent's software project delivery guide positions agents as coordinators for dependencies, execution, blockers, and review, with human-facing outputs that still require inspection.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice signal is that agent workflows need explicit coordination state, blocker handling, and review checkpoints rather than only implementation prompts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for delivery-loop state, blocker triage, dependency ownership, and agent-to-human review packages.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Ingest as workflow evidence only; avoid local vendor coverage.

qualifying_updates.title: Eddyter documents UI requirements for AI-agent products
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Eddyter argued that AI-agent products need editors that support streaming token rendering, tool-call displays, inline diff visualization, code highlighting, long-context conversations, and background-agent changes without corrupting user state.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice update is about application harness UX: agent products need first-class UI patterns for streaming progress, tool evidence, and reviewable diffs.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for streaming agent UI, tool-call rendering, diff review surfaces, and long-context editor state management.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route editor/product catalog facts upstream; keep only the application-pattern requirements locally.
